[compose-substitution] 3 of the variables compose.yaml interpolates are not supplied by the environment
[compose-substitution]   or by .env, so they depend on the engine applying the default after ':-'. Asking the engine…
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution] THIS ENGINE DOES NOT APPLY THE DEFAULTS IN compose.yaml (F-57).
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]   engine:   podman
[compose-substitution]   compose:  podman-compose
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]   These variables would reach the containers as literal placeholder text:
[compose-substitution]     ${GUEST_REGISTRATION_ATTEMPTS_PER_WINDOW:-…}
[compose-substitution]     ${GUEST_REGISTRATION_WINDOW_MINUTES:-…}
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]   What that costs, from the run that found it: the application refuses to start and names
[compose-substitution]   five of them; POSTGRES_USER reaches initdb as punctuation, so the database never
[compose-substitution]   initialises and crash-loops; and the rest are wrong in silence — RESTAURANT_NAME renders
[compose-substitution]   the placeholder as the restaurant's name, an unparseable integer is indistinguishable from
[compose-substitution]   an absent one, and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT arrives non-empty, which turns the exporter
[compose-substitution]   ON and points it at a hostname made of braces.
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]   Two remediations, in order:
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]     1. cp .env.example .env
[compose-substitution]        Every variable compose.yaml interpolates is assigned in that file, so nothing is left
[compose-substitution]        depending on a default. Then run this check again — it will tell you whether it was
[compose-substitution]        enough on your engine, which is not something this repository can know for you.
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]     2. Use a compose that applies defaults:
[compose-substitution]          podman compose …            the Docker Compose provider, if it is installed
[compose-substitution]          pipx install podman-compose a newer release than the distribution's
[compose-substitution]        or export the variables in the shell that runs the stack.
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]   Do not run an instance you care about on an engine that fails this check. Only five of the
[compose-substitution]   affected settings are ones this application validates; the others do not announce themselves.
[compose-substitution] 
[dev-instance] error: this engine does not apply compose.yaml's defaults, so the stack cannot start. Nothing was built (the report above says what to do).

  PUBLIC URL:  https://girls-choose-corner-employed.trycloudflare.com

  • This keeps running after this command exits and after you log out.
    Stop it with:  scripts/dev_instance.sh down
  • Re-running 'up' REUSES this URL. Passkeys registered against it keep
    working. '--new-url' throws it away and mints a new one; every passkey
    registered on the old URL stops matching.
  • Passkeys work here (per-request RP ID, ADR-0005). Password + TOTP is the
    baseline that survives a URL change.
  • Do NOT bootstrap a real, long-lived instance through a quick tunnel.
